summary: Generating Alpha episode with Felix Zulauf, April 2025: career story, top-down political/business cycle process, selective high-conviction trading, weekend chart discipline with fundamentals and technicals, stop-loss and humility, and view that the trade regime break ends globalisation.

claims.speaker: Felix Zulauf
claims.quote: when I saw big risks or big opportunities I went um extreme in my management
claims.claim: Zulauf concentrates and moves to extreme positioning when he sees big risks or opportunities, rather than staying near benchmark constraints.

claims.speaker: Felix Zulauf
claims.quote: I went to 70% cash and 30% in bonds of um commodity companies
claims.claim: At the 1980 commodity boom peak he held a commodity equity fund 70% in cash and 30% in bonds of commodity companies, avoiding the equity bust.
claims.direction: cash and bonds instead of commodity equities

claims.speaker: Felix Zulauf
claims.quote: after 87 uh which was the crash of 87 where I sold all the institutional accounts down to zero equities before it happened
claims.claim: He cut institutional accounts to zero equities before the 1987 crash.

claims.speaker: Felix Zulauf
claims.quote: We used perhaps at times we used 30% leverage and that was all. So, but we were long and short. We could go net 100% short
claims.claim: Zulauf's hedge funds ran long/short with only about 30% leverage but could be net 100% short, so exposure was flexible in both directions.

claims.speaker: Felix Zulauf
claims.quote: I do only enter a position when I have a strong conviction. I'm at the age where I do not have to play. I only play when I see that the odds are turning in my favor
claims.claim: He trades only when odds turn in his favour and otherwise stays out, so selectivity and waiting matter more than being always positioned.

claims.speaker: Felix Zulauf
claims.quote: I try to understand the political setup, the zeitgeist, so to speak, and where we are in the pendulum
claims.claim: Politics swings like a pendulum (left/right, conservative/progressive), and knowing where the pendulum stands helps anticipate political outcomes and their market results.

claims.speaker: Felix Zulauf
claims.quote: these days you have to understand the distortions to the business cycle due to the growing interventions and manipulations by the authorities
claims.claim: Business cycle analysis must adjust for distortions from authorities' interventions, so the cycle is less clean than in the 1960s-70s.
claims.indicator: business cycle adjusted for policy intervention

claims.speaker: Felix Zulauf
claims.quote: from there you deduct you deviate you deviate what it means for interest rates for currencies for capital flows and uh what it means for bonds and equities and the different sectors
claims.claim: The process runs top-down: politics, then business cycle, then implications for rates, currencies and capital flows, and then bonds, equities, defensive vs deep cyclical sectors, currency hedging and commodities.

claims.speaker: Felix Zulauf
claims.quote: when you have a bull market you should not use a 60 or 55 year old portfolio manager because they are conditioned by the previous structural bare market
claims.claim: Portfolio managers are conditioned by the previous regime, so in a new secular bull market an older manager shaped by the preceding bear market will be too cautious; match manager traits to the long cycle.
claims.conditions: Start of a secular bull market

claims.speaker: Felix Zulauf
claims.quote: trade is uh is the most important uh uh variable right now. And and I think the next one issue will probably be capital flows
claims.claim: The key political-market variable in 2025 is trade policy, followed by capital flows.

claims.speaker: Felix Zulauf
claims.quote: it's a similar change of the magnitude of when the wall in Berlin came down or when uh Breton Woods was terminated or when the gold standard was terminated
claims.claim: The Trump trade changes are a regime break comparable to the Berlin Wall, Bretton Woods and the gold standard, ending the globalisation wave of 30 years and creating a more difficult environment for companies.

claims.speaker: Felix Zulauf
claims.quote: it is changing uh the importance and relevance of uh the US dollar as a reserve currency and uh this is changing capital flows and this capital flow will change in principle the level of interest rates in the US
claims.claim: The geopolitical backlash reduces the dollar's reserve role and changes capital flows, which will alter the level of US interest rates.
claims.indicator: USD reserve status; capital flows into US
claims.testable: partly - TIC flows and reserve shares

claims.speaker: Felix Zulauf
claims.quote: the best to overcome the doubts is to have a discipline to have a working discipline
claims.claim: A contrarian is lonely at tops with a bearish view; a fixed analytical routine counters doubt.

claims.speaker: Felix Zulauf
claims.quote: I go through about a thousand charts of uh of money market rates uh bond yields uh currency rates
claims.claim: Every weekend he reviews about 1,000 charts (money market rates, bond yields, 30 currencies, equity and sector indices, the top 100 stocks in US, Europe and Asia) on long, medium and short horizons, for about five hours.
claims.indicator: routine chart review across rates, FX, indices, stocks

claims.speaker: Felix Zulauf
claims.quote: I work a combination of fundamentals to understand the business cycle and where we are and I use technical analysis to support my analysis
claims.claim: Fundamentals set the business-cycle view while technical analysis checks whether the market confirms it and shows the health of the trend.
claims.indicator: technical trend health vs fundamental view

claims.speaker: Felix Zulauf
claims.quote: I also see where the market is not agreeing with my investment thesis. And then I have to dig where where the market does not agree with me
claims.claim: Where price action disagrees with the thesis, he digs deeper for what is wrong; the market's disagreement is a signal to re-examine.

claims.speaker: Felix Zulauf
claims.quote: something that doesn't I have to check. So it's like science you know you you check and whether it's when it's okay you go further and when it's not okay you have to go back to the drawing board
claims.claim: He scans news for items that do not fit his thesis and checks them, treating the thesis like a scientific hypothesis to revise when contradicted.

claims.speaker: Felix Zulauf
claims.quote: there is a failsafe stop-loss that you have to have in place otherwise you know when you lose big it kills you psychologically
claims.claim: Always keep a failsafe stop-loss and stay humble: a large loss unbalances decision-making and is hard to recover.

claims.speaker: Felix Zulauf
claims.quote: when you lose big to make it up is very hard
claims.claim: Large losses are hard to recover (needed gains grow nonlinearly), which matters even more in a performance game.

claims.speaker: Felix Zulauf
claims.quote: I forgot the stop loss and uh and I finally uh killed the position when I was down 50%
claims.claim: His biggest loss was a position held without a stop that was finally closed down 50% when he was about 30.
